title: AF-School-final(B264)
description: Airframe school-final exam (batch 264) covering structures, wood and fabric, welding and sheet metal, composites, weight and balance, landing gear, fuel, air conditioning, pneumatics and pressurization.

questions.question: Which rivet type is used on the upper surface of a wing and stabilizer?
questions.explanation: The source identifies the flat head rivet for the upper wing and stabilizer surfaces, where a low profile is wanted.

questions.question: What do cyclic temperature variation and humidity cause in a wood structure?
questions.explanation: Repeated swings in temperature and moisture make the wood swell and shrink, stressing and eventually breaking down the glue joints.

questions.question: What does a blue stain in wood indicate?
options: B. A sapwood defect (fungal stain in the sapwood)
C. Excess resin in the wood
questions.explanation: Blue stain is a discoloration of the sapwood caused by fungus, and it is treated as a wood defect to evaluate.

questions.question: Who issues the Type Certificate Data Sheet (TCDS)?
questions.explanation: The TCDS is issued by the aviation authority (the FAA) and records the approved specifications and limitations of the type design.

questions.question: What kind of item is a CDCCL (Critical Design Configuration Control Limitation)?
options: A. A non-routine item (a configuration control requirement, not a periodic inspection)
B. A routine daily inspection item
questions.explanation: A CDCCL is a configuration control limitation that must be preserved during maintenance or alterations; it is not a routine periodic inspection.

questions.question: Which type of structural load, other than tension and compression, acts on aircraft structure?
questions.explanation: Besides tension and compression, aircraft structures also carry bending, shear, and torsion loads. Bending is the one named in the source.

questions.question: How long should reinforcing tape be relative to the fabric member it covers?
options: A. Slightly more than (longer or wider than) the member it covers
B. Exactly the same size with no overlap
C. Much shorter than the member
questions.explanation: Reinforcing tape is cut slightly larger than the rib cap or member so that it fully covers and protects the attachment area.

questions.question: What is used to attach fabric to the aircraft structure?
questions.explanation: Fabric cement bonds the fabric covering to the airframe structure, usually reinforced with stitching and tape.

questions.question: What happens when air enters an insulation blanket?
options: A. It decreases the insulation efficiency
B. It increases the insulation efficiency
C. It has no effect on insulation
questions.explanation: Air movement or moisture inside the blanket reduces its ability to resist heat and sound transfer.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an input to the weight and balance analysis in a computer?
options: C. Moment (it is calculated from weight and arm, not entered)
questions.explanation: A weight and balance program takes weights and arms as inputs and calculates the moments from them.

questions.question: A 50 kg weight is added aft of the CG. What happens to the CG?
options: C. The CG does not change
questions.explanation: Adding weight behind the existing CG increases the aft moment, which shifts the overall CG rearward.

questions.question: Which welding process uses a non-consumable electrode?
questions.explanation: GTAW (TIG) uses a non-consumable tungsten electrode, with filler metal added separately if needed.

questions.question: What is the formula for the CG location?
options: A. CG = total weight / total moment
B. CG = total weight x total moment
C. CG = total moment / total weight
questions.explanation: The CG location is found by dividing the sum of all moments by the sum of all weights.

questions.question: What type of load acts on the upper surface of a wing in flight?
questions.explanation: As the wing bends upward under lift, its upper skin is compressed while the lower skin is stretched in tension.

questions.question: In a vapor cycle cooling system, which component raises refrigerant from low pressure and temperature to high pressure and temperature?
questions.explanation: The compressor compresses the refrigerant vapor, raising both its pressure and temperature.

questions.question: In a vapor cycle cooling system, which component changes the refrigerant vapor into liquid?
questions.explanation: The condenser removes heat from the high-pressure vapor so that it condenses into a liquid.

questions.question: In a vapor cycle cooling system, which component rejects heat to the surroundings?
questions.explanation: The condenser releases the heat absorbed by the refrigerant to the surrounding air.

questions.question: What type of ducts are used to supply conditioned air in the cabin?
options: A. Hot stainless steel ducts only
questions.explanation: Conditioned air at moderate temperature can be carried in plastic ducting, which can be rigid or flexible.

questions.question: What is the clamp with two wood blocks used in wood bonding called?
questions.explanation: A caul is a clamping aid, usually a pair of wood blocks, used to spread pressure evenly over a glue joint.

questions.question: What flame results from burning more acetylene than oxygen?
questions.explanation: Excess acetylene produces a carburizing (reducing) flame with a feathery inner cone.

questions.question: What is a disadvantage of AVGAS?
questions.explanation: AVGAS is highly volatile, so it is easily lost through evaporation.

questions.question: What property makes turbine fuel different from AVGAS?
questions.explanation: Kerosene-type turbine fuel has a higher boiling point and flash point than gasoline, so it evaporates less.

questions.question: How is a CG problem fixed?
options: A. By adding more fuel only
B. By shifting cargo and other loads
questions.explanation: A CG outside limits is corrected by repositioning cargo, baggage, and other loads.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the torque link on a landing gear strut?
options: A. To keep the wheel aligned by stopping the lower cylinder from rotating relative to the upper cylinder
B. To absorb all vertical landing shock
C. To lock the gear down
questions.explanation: Torque links connect the upper and lower strut cylinders so that the wheel stays aligned while the strut compresses and extends.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the chine on an aircraft tire?
options: A. To increase tire traction on dry runways
questions.explanation: A chine is a molded deflector that throws runway water to the side, protecting the engines and airframe from spray.

questions.question: How does landing gear cushion (dump) the landing impact?
options: A. By increasing the impact time
B. By decreasing the impact time
C. By making the gear rigid
questions.explanation: Spreading the impact over a longer time lowers the peak force transmitted to the airframe.

questions.question: What is a means of reducing parasite drag from the landing gear?
questions.explanation: Retracting the gear into the airframe in flight removes it from the airstream and cuts parasite drag.

questions.question: Which landing gear type dissipates landing energy into the atmosphere?
questions.explanation: In the source's answer, the spring oleo strut forces fluid through an orifice, turning the landing energy into heat that is released to the air.

questions.question: Which statement about knock and detonation is wrong?
options: A. That detonation has a cockpit indication but knock does not
B. That detonation can damage the engine
C. That fuel octane rating affects knock resistance
questions.explanation: The source marks this statement as the incorrect one among the choices.

questions.question: Which material are SAE 4130 landing gear structural parts made from?
questions.explanation: SAE 4130 is a chromium-molybdenum alloy steel widely used for strong, weldable aircraft structure.

questions.question: What is the effect of ice accumulation on an aircraft?
options: A. It increases lift and reduces drag
B. It reduces lift and increases drag
C. It has no effect on performance
questions.explanation: Ice disturbs airflow over the wing, lowering lift and raising drag, and it adds weight.

questions.question: What type of waste disposal system is used on light aircraft?
options: C. A gray water recirculation system
questions.explanation: Small aircraft typically use a simple self-contained lavatory instead of a central vacuum system.

questions.question: Why is a 25-hour inspection of the fuel system performed?
options: A. It is required for all aircraft after every flight
B. It is critical for a new aircraft and engine
C. It is only done at overhaul
questions.explanation: A 25-hour check of the fuel system is emphasized for new aircraft and engines, when early leaks and loose fittings are most likely.

questions.question: If the top of a wheel tilts outboard (away from the aircraft), what is it called?
questions.explanation: Positive camber means the top of the wheel leans outward; negative camber means it leans inward.

questions.question: Which two alignments are very important for the wings of an airplane?
options: A. Angle of incidence and dihedral angle
B. Sweep angle and aspect ratio
questions.explanation: Wing rigging focuses on angle of incidence and dihedral because both strongly affect flight characteristics.

questions.question: What is a composite that contains two or more different reinforcing materials in the same matrix commonly known as?
questions.explanation: Mixing different reinforcement fibers within one resin matrix is called a hybrid composite.

questions.question: Which honeycomb core cell size provides better support for sandwich face sheets?
options: B. Cell size has no effect
questions.explanation: Smaller cells support the thin face sheets at closer intervals and resist dimpling better.

questions.question: What is a composite made of thin metal sheets bonded to a thick honeycomb core called?
questions.explanation: Thin skins bonded to a thick lightweight core form a sandwich construction.

questions.question: Which core cell shape is used to make panels with complex curves?
questions.explanation: Bell-shaped (flexible) cells let the core bend into compound curves.

questions.question: What is used to impregnate dry fibers with resin for a wet layup?
questions.explanation: A squeegee works the resin through the dry fabric and removes the excess.

questions.question: Which reinforcing fiber has high impact resistance?
questions.explanation: Aramid fiber is known for its toughness and high impact resistance.

questions.question: What tool is used to remove a burr from the edge of a sheet or to deburr a hole?
questions.explanation: A deburring tool is made to take burrs off sheet edges and drilled holes.

questions.question: When a sheet metal part has intersecting bend radii, what should be done?
options: A. Remove material (drill relief holes at the intersection)
B. Bend both radii without any relief
questions.explanation: Material must be removed, usually by relief holes, so the metal does not pile up or crack where the bends meet.

questions.question: How is rivet spacing (pitch) measured?
options: A. From edge to edge of the rivet heads
B. Between the centerlines of rivets in the same row
C. From the sheet edge to the nearest rivet
questions.explanation: Rivet pitch is the distance between the centerlines of adjacent rivets in the same row.

questions.question: What is the consequence of too much torque in a pneumatic system?
options: A. Better sealing with no downside
C. Damage to the metal fittings and seals
questions.explanation: Over-torquing can crack or distort fittings and damage seals, which causes leaks.

questions.question: What is a high-pressure air source for a pneumatic system?
questions.explanation: Multi-piston compressors can build the high pressures needed for high-pressure pneumatic systems.

questions.question: What is the RAT (Ram Air Turbine) used for?
options: A. Flight control power if the hydraulic system fails
C. Charging the passenger oxygen system
questions.explanation: The RAT drops into the airstream and supplies emergency hydraulic or electrical power for essential flight controls.

questions.question: Which fastener is commonly used to obtain a flush surface in a fuel tank?
questions.explanation: The source names E-Z Buck as the fastener used for a flush surface in fuel tank areas.

questions.question: Which component in the spoiler control system can be commanded by the spoiler control module?
questions.explanation: The spoiler control module sends its commands to the power control actuators, which move the spoilers.

questions.question: Which glue, when exposed to moist conditions with swell and shrink stress, deteriorates and eventually fails, and is obsolete for aircraft repair?
questions.explanation: Urea formaldehyde breaks down under moisture and cycling stress, so it is considered obsolete for aircraft repair.

questions.question: On the Boeing 737, which pumps take fluid from the standpipe for System A and System B?
options: A. System A EDP, System B EDP, and the EMDP
B. Only the System A EDP
questions.explanation: The source states that both engine-driven pumps and the electric motor-driven pump draw from the standpipe.

questions.question: Which unit aligns the nose gear before it retracts?
questions.explanation: A centering cam straightens the nose wheel as the strut extends so it fits the wheel well on retraction.

questions.question: Which bleeding method is most used for a power brake system?
questions.explanation: The source gives top-to-bottom as the usual way to bleed a power brake system.

questions.question: How is a landing gear down-and-locked position shown in the cockpit?
questions.explanation: A green light for each gear shows it is down and locked.

questions.question: What does a red light in the landing gear indication mean?
options: A. The gear is in transit
B. The gear is down and locked
C. The gear is fully retracted and locked
questions.explanation: A red (unsafe) light is shown while the gear is moving between positions or not locked.

questions.question: Which unit interfaces with the pilot control transducers and controls primary flight control actuation?
questions.explanation: The ACE receives the pilot input signals and drives the primary flight control actuators.

questions.question: What types of selector valve are there?
questions.explanation: Selector valves are commonly built with poppet, cone, or disk elements.

questions.question: What is the lowest cabin altitude that can be selected for pressurization?
questions.explanation: The source gives 1,000 ft below sea level as the lowest selectable altitude.

questions.question: What happens when the maximum differential pressure is reached?
options: A. The system maintains the maximum differential pressure
B. The cabin dumps all pressure
C. The outflow valve closes completely
questions.explanation: At the limit, the controller holds the maximum differential pressure while the aircraft continues to climb.

questions.question: At what cabin altitude does the cabin altitude red light go off?
questions.explanation: The source gives 8,500 ft as the point at which the warning light goes out as cabin altitude returns below it.
